subject: AI & Agents
title: How Recommendation Engines Work
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Recommendation Engines Work.

hook.text: Netflix somehow knows you'll love a Korean thriller you've never heard of. How?

buildup.text: Recommendation engines compare your behavior to millions of similar users.

discovery.text: If people like you loved something, odds are you will too. It's collaborative filtering.

twist.text: It creates filter bubbles — you see more of what you already like and less of everything else.

climax.text: YouTube's algorithm drives 70% of watch time. It decides what the world pays attention to.

punchline.text: It doesn't know your taste — it knows your tribe's.

quiz.question: What is collaborative filtering?
options: Recommending items based on similar users' preferences

details.summary: Recommendation engines analyze user behavior and item features to suggest what you might like next. They power Netflix suggestions, Spotify playlists, and Amazon product recommendations using collaborative filtering.
details.whyItMatters: Recommendation engines shape what billions of people watch, listen to, and buy daily. Understanding their logic reveals why you see certain content and how filter bubbles form.
takeaways: Recommendations are based on user behavior and item similarity
Collaborative filtering matches you with users who share your taste
These systems shape media consumption for billions of people

faq.question: How does Netflix know what I want to watch?
faq.answer: Netflix tracks what you watch, how long you watch, and what you skip. It compares your patterns with millions of similar users and recommends shows that people with your taste profile enjoyed.

faq.question: Can recommendation engines create filter bubbles?
faq.answer: Yes. By showing you more of what you already like, they can narrow your exposure to new ideas and perspectives. This is a known problem that platforms address with some diversity in their recommendations.
